LORAJEAN A. ALAMIN Officer-in-Charge Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for General Administration Office of the President Malacanang Dear OIC Alamin: This has reference to your letter dated March 30, 2022 forwarding to the Department, for comment and recommendation the letter dated January 7, 2022 from Mr. Christian H. Nabella addressed to His Excellency, President Rodrigo Duterte, relative to Resolution No. 245, s. 2021 of the Sanggunian Panlungsod of the City of Carcar, Province of Cebu, requesting the issuance of an Executive Order authorizing the utilization of their Economic Development Fund and other source of funds in the form of housing materials to help the constituents whose dwellings were greatly devastated by Super Typhoon Odette. Per the mentioned Resolution, the Super Typhoon Odette badly damaged 80% of the houses in Carcar and that the City's calamity fund is not enough for the people to recoüer. Thus, the Sanggunian Panlungsod of Carcar resolved to request the President to issue an Executive Order utilizing their Development Fund (DF) as housing materials to their constituents whose dwellings were greatly devastated by the said typhoon. At the outset, attention is invited to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), Department of Finance (DOF), and this Department's Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 01 , dated November 4, 2020 prescribing the revised guidelines on the appropriation and utilization of the 20% Development Fund. Said JMC provides for the development projects that may be included under the 20% Development Fund, thus: "3.2.1. The 20% DF shall be utilized to finance the LGU's priority development projects, as embodied in their respective duly approved local development plans, and medium-term and annual investment programs, which should be harmonized with Regional Development Plan and the Philippine Development plan." 3.2.2 The development projects that may be included under the 20% DF shall be those that are necessary, appropriate, or incidental to efficient and effective local governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people." (Emphasis supplied) "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

It is worthy to note that the JMC no longer prescribes the specific allowable development projects that may be funded by the LGUs out of their respective 20% DFs. Instead, said JMC sets the general policies and guidelines to be observed by LGUs in identifying and implementing development projects to be funded under the 20% DF, including the prescription of the prohibited expenditure items. 1 Item 3.2.2. of the DBM-DOF-DILG JMC essentially covers a wide array of programs, projects, activities (PPAs), or expenses which the LGUs may deem as "necessary, appropriate, or incidental to the efficient and effective local governance, and essential to the promotion of the general welfare of the people."2 The DBM emphasized that it is the LGUs concerned that are in a better position to determine the said PPAs and expenses that may be charged against their respective 20% DFs, as long as the same do not fall within the purview of the list of expenditure items not allowed to be charged against the DF as enumerated in item 3.2.5 of DBM-DOF-DILG JMC No. 1.3 From the foregoing, if the City of Carcar deems the giving of aid through the rehabilitation of the affected dwellings as necessary and essential to the promotion of the general welfare of their constituents, then the same may be funded under their 20% DF. The City of Carcar is in a better position to determine the essential needs of its constituents which are necessary for the promotion of the general welfare especially in times of calamities. However, the proposed programs, projects, and activities that may fall under any of the expenditure items specified under item 3.2.5 of the said JMC are not allowed to be charged against the 20% DF.4 Thank you. Respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Under retary for Local Government OSEC/EMA/LLLS-L LD/ m/clp 1 Letter reply dated 24 March 2022 from Director John Aries S.
